explanation.text: The Logic: Gamma is defined as the rate of change of an option's delta with respect to the underlying price. It is a second-order Greek that captures how quickly the option's directional exposure shifts as the underlying moves. The Trap: Time decay is theta, volatility sensitivity is vega, and interest-rate sensitivity is rho. Each Greek measures a distinct dimension of option risk. Note: The Portfolio Managers (NISM-Series-XXI-B) workbook lists gamma alongside delta and vega as option-based sensitivity measures but does not explicitly define gamma as the rate of change of delta. The definition above reflects general industry/regulatory knowledge of option Greeks.
